newsitem.title: USA: Orange County files should be sealed-Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Orange County files should be sealed-Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co has asked an Orange County, Calif., judge to keep county grand jury transcripts sealed in part because prosecutors suggested that the company's employees may have broken the law, the Orange County Register reported Friday.

In a brief filed with Superior Court Judge David Carter, Merrill Lynch lawyers said 28 employees testified before the grand jury, providing confidential information on dealings with the company's clients, the newspaper reported.
Prosecutors assured the company that the transcripts would remain sealed if there was no indictment, the brief stated.

Merrill Lynch attorneys said the transcripts contain information damaging to its employees' reputations, "including suggestions by the DA, through questioning, that individuals may have been engaged in unlawful or improper conduct," according to the Register.

"The witnesses gave highly confidential, proprietary information," wrote Costa Mesa lawyer Paul Meyer, representing Merrill Lynch, in a court declaration. "Proprietary information, if revealed, would be of great interest and advantage to Merrill Lynch's competitors."
The brief was filed under seal but Carter unsealed it Thursday. A copy of the brief was not immediately available.
Orange County attorneys and prosecutors clashed this week over the grand jury transcripts, which could shed light on Merrill Lynch's role in the county bankruptcy crisis.
The grand jury investigation ended in June when Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $30 million. The deal ensured Merrill Lynch and its employees would not face criminal charges.
Lawyers for the county asked Carter earlier this week to give them access to the transcripts for use in the county's $2 billion-plus civil lawsuit against Merrill Lynch.
County prosecutors maintain that the grand jury documents must remain sealed because no indictments were returned by the panel.
A court hearing has been set for July 30 to debate the issue.
